column1: Katharine L. Shester reviews a book by Jason Barr about the development of New York City
column2: 凯瑟琳·L. 谢斯特评论杰森·巴尔一本有关纽约市发展的著作。

column1: In Building the Skyline, Jason Barr takes the reader through a detailed history of New York City.
column2: 在《构筑天际线》中，杰森·巴尔带读者详细回顾了纽约市的历史。
column3: takes the reader through|带领某人详细了解

column1: The book combines geology, history, economics, and a lot of data to explain why business clusters developed where they did and how the early decisions of workers and firms shaped the skyline we see today.
column2: 本书结合地质学、历史、经济学和大量数据，解释了商业为何会在特定地点集聚，以及工人和企业早期的决定如何塑造了我们今天看到的天际线。

column1: Building the Skyline is organized into two distinct parts.
column2: 《构筑天际线》分为两个截然不同的部分。

column1: The first is primarily historical and addresses New York’s settlement and growth from 1609 to 1900; the second deals primarily with the 20th century and is a compilation of chapters commenting on different aspects of New York’s urban development.
column2: 第一部分主要讲历史，探讨纽约从1609年到1900年的定居开发和成长。第二部分主要讲20世纪，由若干章组成，分别评述纽约城市发展的不同方面。

column1: The tone and organization of the book changes somewhat between the first and second parts, as the latter chapters incorporate aspects of Barr’s related research papers.
column2: 这两部分的语调和结构有所变化，因为后半部的各章融入了巴尔相关研究论文的部分内容。

column1: Barr begins chapter one by taking the reader on a ‘helicopter time-machine’ ride – giving a fascinating account of how the New York landscape in 1609 might have looked from the sky.
column2: 在第一章开头，巴尔让读者搭上“直升机时光机”，把1609年的纽约从空中俯瞰可能是何种景象，描绘得引人入胜。

column1: He then moves on to a subterranean walking tour of the city, indicating the location of rock and water below the subsoil, before taking the reader back to the surface.
column2: 随后，他带着读者在城市地下步行游览，指出底土之下岩石和水所在的位置，再带大家回到地面。

column1: His love of the city comes through as he describes various fun facts about the location of the New York residence of early 19th-century vice-president Aaron Burr as well as a number of legends about the city.
column2: 巴尔对纽约的热爱，在他说起各种趣闻时自然流露。他讲到19世纪初美国副总统阿伦·伯尔在纽约的居所位置，也谈到这座城市的一些传说。

column1: Chapters two and three take the reader up to the Civil War (1861–1865), with chapter two focusing on the early development of land and the implementation of a grid system in 1811.
column2: 第二和第三章把读者带到了美国内战（1861至1865年）时期，其中第二章着重讨论早期土地开发以及1811年方格路网规划的实施。

column1: Chapter three focuses on land use before the Civil War.
column2: 第三章着重讨论内战前的土地利用。

column1: Both chapters are informative and well researched and set the stage for the economic analysis that comes later in the book.
column2: 这两章都内容丰富、考证扎实，为本书后面的经济分析作了铺垫。
column5: set the stage for|为……作铺垫

column1: I would have liked Barr to expand upon his claim that existing tenements* prevented skyscrapers in certain neighborhoods because ‘likely no skyscraper developer was interested in performing the necessary “slum clearance”’.
column2: 我希望巴尔把这个论点讲得更详细些：他认为，某些街区已有的多户住宅*妨碍了摩天大楼的兴建，因为“很可能没有任何摩天大楼开发商愿意进行必要的‘贫民区清拆’”。
column6: tenements|n. 多户住宅；廉租公寓楼

column1: Later in the book, Barr makes the claim that the depth of bedrock** was not a limiting factor for developers, as foundation costs were a small fraction of the cost of development.
column2: 在书的后面，巴尔又提出，基岩**的深度并没有限制开发商，因为地基成本只占开发成本的很小一部分。
column9: a small fraction of|……的很小一部分

column1: At first glance, it is not obvious why slum clearance would be limiting, while more expensive foundations would not.
column2: 乍看之下，并不清楚为什么清拆贫民区会成为限制，而更昂贵的地基工程却不会。

column1: Chapter four focuses on immigration and the location of neighborhoods and tenements in the late 19th century.
column2: 第四章关注19世纪后期的移民和各街区、多户住宅的空间分布。

column1: Barr identifies four primary immigrant enclaves and analyzes their locations in terms of the amenities available in the area.
column2: 巴尔列出四个主要移民聚居区，并从当地有哪些生活设施的角度分析它们的选址。

column1: Most of these enclaves were located on the least valuable land, between the industries located on the waterfront and the wealthy neighborhoods bordering Central Park.
column2: 这些聚居区大多位于价值最低的土地上，夹在滨水地带的工业区与中央公园旁的富裕街区之间。

column1: Part two of the book begins with a discussion of the economics of skyscraper height.
column2: 本书第二部分以摩天大楼高度的经济学讨论开篇。

column1: In chapter five, Barr distinguishes between engineering height, economic height, and developer height — where engineering height is the tallest building that can be safely made at a given time, economic height is the height that is most efficient from society’s point of view, and developer height is the actual height chosen by the developer, who is attempting to maximize return on investment.
column2: 在第五章，巴尔区分了三种高度：工程高度、经济高度和开发商高度。工程高度是指在某一时期能够安全建造的最高建筑高度；经济高度是从社会整体角度看效率最高的建筑高度。开发商高度则是开发商为使投资回报最大化而实际选择的建筑高度。
column7: at a given time|在某一时期
column9: society’s point of view|社会整体的角度

column1: Chapter five also has an interesting discussion of the technological advances that led to the construction of skyscrapers.
column2: 第五章还有一段有趣的讨论，介绍了促使摩天大楼得以建成的技术进步。

column1: For example, the introduction of iron and steel skeletal frames made thick, load-bearing walls unnecessary, expanding the usable square footage of buildings and increasing the use of windows and availability of natural light.
column2: 例如，采用铁、钢骨架后，建筑物不再需要厚重的承重墙，可用面积随之增加，也能多装窗户，有更多自然光照进来。
column7: usable square footage|可用建筑面积

column1: Chapter six then presents data on building height throughout the 20th century and uses regression analysis to ‘predict’ building construction.
column2: 接下来的第六章给出整个20世纪的建筑高度数据，并使用回归分析来“预测”建筑物的兴建。

column1: While less technical than the research paper on which the chapter is based, it is probably more technical than would be preferred by a general audience.
column2: 虽然这一章的技术性不及其所依据的研究论文，但对普通读者而言，大概仍比他们希望看到的更专业。

column1: Chapter seven tackles the ‘bedrock myth’, the assumption that the absence of bedrock close to the surface between Downtown and Midtown New York is the reason for skyscrapers not being built between the two urban centers.
column2: 第七章探讨了“基岩迷思”：有人认为，纽约下城和中城之间没有靠近地表的基岩，因此这两处市中心地段之间才没有建造摩天大楼。

column1: Rather, Barr argues that while deeper bedrock does increase foundation costs, these costs were neither prohibitively high nor were they large compared to the overall cost of building a skyscraper.
column2: 巴尔的观点则是，基岩较深确实会增加地基成本，但这笔钱既没有高到令开发商却步，相较于建造一座摩天大楼的总成本，也不算多。

column1: What I enjoyed the most about this chapter was Barr’s discussion of how foundations are actually built.
column2: 我最喜欢本章中巴尔对地基实际上如何建造的讨论。

column1: He describes the use of caissons, which enable workers to dig down for considerable distances, often below the water table, until they reach bedrock.
column2: 他描述了沉箱的用途：工人借助沉箱可以向下挖得很深，常常要挖到地下水位以下，直到抵达基岩。

column1: Barr’s thorough technological history discusses not only how caissons work, but also the dangers involved.
column2: 巴尔这段翔实的技术史不但解释沉箱怎样工作，也说明了其中的危险。

column1: While this chapter references empirical research papers, it is a relatively easy read.
column2: 尽管本章引用了实证研究论文，读起来却相对轻松。
column7: easy read|读起来轻松的文章

column1: Chapters eight and nine focus on the birth of Midtown and the building boom of the 1920s.
column2: 第八和第九章关注纽约中城的诞生和20世纪20年代的建筑热潮。

column1: Chapter eight contains lengthy discussions of urban economic theory that may serve as a distraction to readers primarily interested in New York.
column2: 第八章花了很大篇幅讨论城市经济理论。对于主要想了解纽约的读者，这些内容可能会让他们觉得偏离了主题。
column5: urban economic theory|城市经济理论
column6: distraction|n. 分散注意力的事物

column1: However, they would be well-suited for undergraduates learning about the economics of cities.
column2: 不过，对于学习城市经济学的本科生，这些讨论会很合适。

column1: In the next chapter, Barr considers two of the primary explanations for the building boom of the 1920s — the first being exuberance, and the second being financing.
column2: 在下一章中，巴尔考察了对20世纪20年代建筑热潮的两种主要解释：一是市场情绪高涨，二是融资。

column1: He uses data to assess the viability of these two explanations and finds that supply and demand factors explain much of the development of the 1920s; though it enabled the boom, cheap credit was not, he argues, the primary cause.
column2: 他用数据检验这两种解释是否站得住脚，发现供求因素可以解释20世纪20年代相当一部分开发活动；他认为，廉价信贷虽为繁荣创造了条件，却并非首要原因。

column1: In the final chapter (chapter 10), Barr discusses another of his empirical papers that estimates Manhattan land values from the mid-19th century to the present day.
column2: 在最后一章，也就是第十章，巴尔讨论了他的另一篇实证研究论文；文中估算了从19世纪中叶到今天曼哈顿的地价。

column1: The data work that went into these estimations is particularly impressive.
column2: 这些估算背后所做的数据处理工作格外令人印象深刻。

column1: Toward the end of the chapter, Barr assesses ‘whether skyscrapers are a cause or an effect of high land values’.
column2: 在这章临近结尾时，巴尔评估了一个问题：“摩天大楼究竟是高地价的原因，还是高地价的结果？”
column3: Toward the end of|在……快结束时

column1: He finds that changes in land values predict future building height, but the reverse is not true.
column2: 他发现，地价的变化可以预测未来的建筑高度，但反过来却不成立。
column5: future building height|未来的建筑高度

column1: The book ends with an epilogue, in which Barr discusses the impact of climate change on the city and makes policy suggestions for New York going forward.
column2: 本书以一篇结语收尾。巴尔在其中讨论了气候变化对纽约市的影响，也对该市今后的政策提出了建议。
